title: Before Model Escalation: Contracts, Instructions, and Outcomes in Browser Agents
why: Compares action schemas and runtime instructions for BrowserGym agents, including status-vs-page-effect mismatches and a failed escalation controller.
mechanism: Browser-agent action space and feedback: compares legacy vs conditional action schemas against explicit runtime instructions, and audits cases where returned action status disagrees with observed page effects; a failed observation-aware escalation controller is retained as a negative result.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: in a Ministral 14B schema-by-instruction factorial, original instructions yield 45/60 vs 49/60 with conditional schemas; explicit runtime instructions reach 51/60 in each arm (3 unique successes each). A failed observation-aware escalation controller scored 56/72 vs 66/72 for a stronger fixed policy. BrowserGym 0.14.3 exporter/executor tests show mismatches; a 500→5000 ms deadline intervention removed timeouts in a 23-case repeated study.

title: pixeltree: distilling "look at the screen" into a small local model — what worked, what did not
why: Builds a 19 MB screenshot-to-element-tree for Linux desktop GUI agents and tests when the tree helps task success.
mechanism: Perception for desktop GUI agents: a 19 MB YOLO11s detector plus OCR turns a screenshot into a text element tree; a Linux desktop testbench then compares screenshot-only, tree-only, screenshot+tree, and system AT-SPI observations.
evaluation_signal: Author-reported: on 48 programmatically graded tasks in 8 unseen Linux apps, Claude Haiku was 86% screenshot-only vs 57% tree-only and 81% screenshot+tree (no gain). GLM 5.3 Flash was 41/48 with screenshot+tree vs 34/48 screenshot-only. Detector class-agnostic F1 0.854 on 10 held-out Linux apps, vs OmniParser v2 detector 0.586 on the same exam. Negative results include a tree-first policy and a cleaning rule that broke close buttons.
